summary: This proposed standard defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for network management, with objects for configuring and monitoring the Neighborhood Discovery Protocol (NHDP). It replaces RFC 6779 with revisions and extensions to that earlier document.

eli5.summary: A MIB is a list of dials and meters that lets you check and adjust a network device. This lists the dials and meters for the protocol that lets nearby devices discover their neighbors.

subtitle: The SNMP MIB module for configuring and monitoring the MANET Neighborhood Discovery Protocol on a router.

tldr.problem: Operators of ad hoc networks need a standard way to configure, watch and troubleshoot the Neighborhood Discovery Protocol (NHDP) running on their routers.
tldr.mechanism: The NHDP-MIB module defines configuration, state and performance objects plus rate-limited notifications, all reachable over SNMP. Tables record the local interfaces, 1-hop neighbors and 2-hop neighbors.
tldr.outcome: RFC 7939 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 6779, adding support for the NHDP optimization of RFC 7466.

today: RFC 7939 is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It replaced RFC 6779 as the MIB specification for RFC 6130.

sections.title: What the NHDP-MIB Is For
sections.content:
RFC 7939 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for use with network management protocols. The MIB module, named NHDP-MIB, describes objects for configuring parameters of the Mobile Ad Hoc Network (MANET) Neighborhood Discovery Protocol (NHDP) process on a router, as defined in RFC 6130. It also reports state, performance information and notifications, which helps troubleshoot problems during neighbor discovery.

NHDP lets a router discover and track routers up to two hops away by exchanging HELLO messages. Routing and multicast flooding protocols built in the IETF MANET working group can use that information.

This document obsoletes RFC 6779. The change is necessary because RFC 7466 updated NHDP. It adds the objects nhdpIib2HopSetN2Lost and nhdpIfPerfCounterDiscontinuityTime, adds the value notconsidered to nhdp2HopNbrState, and revises the full compliance statement.
sections.eli5: Routers that find each other without a fixed setup need a way for humans to check on them. This document defines the standard list of settings and readings for that job.

sections.title: How the MIB Module Is Organized
sections.content:
The module is built from three parts: nhdpNotifications, nhdpObjects and nhdpConformance. The objects are split into three groups.

  • The Configuration Group holds the controls for the NHDP instance. It tries to support every configuration object defined in RFC 6130, with the same constraints and default values.
  • The State Group reports the current state, covering the information bases defined in Sections 6, 7 and 8 of RFC 6130.
  • The Performance Group holds values that can be polled to compute histories or watch how often sets change. Unstable neighbors and frequent changes can hurt NHDP performance.

nhdpConformance defines the minimal and maximal conformance requirements for implementations.
sections.eli5: The control panel has three areas: dials to set things, meters to show what is happening now, and counters that show whether things are stable.

sections.title: Notifications and Throttling
sections.content:
A router can send notifications when an event happens, so a manager does not have to poll many routers. The module defines three: nhdpNbrStateChange, nhdp2HopNbrStateChange and nhdpIfStateChange. Each carries the interface name and the new state or status, so the source can be identified.

Because a flood of notifications can overload a lossy wireless network, the RFC suggests three mechanisms similar to those of RFC 4750.

  • Ignore initial activity. A router SHOULD NOT originate expected notifications for a configured interval after NHDP starts. The interval is RECOMMENDED to be at least 3 times nhdpHelloInterval.
  • Throttle. The number of notifications per time window is bounded. Because NHDP is expected on lossier channels than OSPF, the threshold is RECOMMENDED to be lower than the 7 traps in 10 seconds recommended for OSPF; the RFC recommends a threshold of 10 changes and a window of at least 5 times nhdpHelloInterval.
  • One notification per event.
sections.eli5: If every little change rang a bell, the bell would never stop at start-up. So the router waits a bit before ringing, and rings only when many things change in a short time.

sections.title: Tables and Indexing
sections.content:
The module has tables for the local router, a local MANET interface, 1-hop neighbors, interfaces on those neighbors, and 2-hop neighbors. Examples are nhdpInterfaceTable (interface configuration), nhdpIibLinkSetTable (links to 1-hop neighbors), nhdpIib2HopSetTable (symmetric 2-hop neighbors) and nhdpNibNeighborSetTable (addresses of 1-hop neighbors). Matching performance tables record measurements for interfaces, discovered neighbor interfaces, neighbors and 2-hop neighbors.

Tables are indexed with three constructs: nhdpIfIndex (the local interface), nhdpDiscIfIndex (a locally managed index for a known interface on a neighbor) and nhdpDiscRouterIndex (a locally managed index for a known neighbor router).

The last two exist because SMIv2 cannot index tables by variable address sets. They are defined as textual conventions, NeighborIfIndex and NeighborRouterIndex. The router may not know that two address sets belong to one interface, so several indexes can point to the same real neighbor interface. The local MIB agent manages, aggregates and retires these indexes as it learns more.
sections.eli5: Each neighbor gets a local nickname, like a number on a name tag, because the router cannot always tell which addresses belong to the same device. The router's own list of nicknames can change as it learns more.

sections.title: Relationship to Other MIB Modules
sections.content:
The NHDP-MIB does not duplicate the System Group of the SNMPv2-MIB. Its nhdpInterfaceTable sparse-augments the ifTable of the Interfaces Group MIB, so each entry has a matching interface entry where nhdpIfIndex equals ifIndex. If the interface entry is deleted, the NHDP entry is deleted too, NHDP is disabled on that interface, and the related configuration and state are removed.

Routing protocol MIB modules that rely on NHDP can share the two neighbor index conventions. They are locally significant but should be common to the NHDP-MIB and the routing protocol MIB on the same router, which improves cross-referencing of information. The module imports definitions from SNMPv2-SMI, SNMPv2-TC, SNMPv2-CONF, IF-MIB, SNMP-FRAMEWORK-MIB, INET-ADDRESS-MIB and FLOAT-TC-MIB.
sections.eli5: The NHDP panel plugs into the other standard panels on the same router, and they use the same nicknames for neighbors, so you can match up their readings.

sections.title: Where the MIB Is Used
sections.content:
The applicability statement gives three example MANET scenarios where standards-based management is useful.

  • Parking lot initial configuration: vehicles that form the MANET are configured from a fixed Network Operations Center (NOC) at a staging site before deployment.
  • Mobile vehicles with a low-bandwidth satellite link: monitoring and fault management from a fixed NOC.
  • Fixed NOC and a mobile local manager in larger vehicles: hierarchical management, with central and local roles.
sections.eli5: Three examples: setting up trucks in a parking lot, checking on moving trucks over a slow satellite link, and having both a head office and a driver-side helper in the same big truck.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Some objects are writable and therefore sensitive. nhdpIfStatus turns NHDP on or off for an interface, and disabling it would break routing and cause network-wide disruption. nhdpHelloInterval, nhdpHelloMinInterval and nhdpRefreshInterval control the HELLO rate, and too high a rate could overload interface resources. The link quality objects, such as nhdpHystAcceptQuality, can destabilize the network if set badly. All writable objects are in nhdpInterfaceTable.

Readable objects can also be sensitive. nhdpDiscIfSetTable lists addresses of discovered neighbors, which gives an adversary broad information about the MANET members in one place.

Because MANETs are often used for emergency services or military tactical applications, the RFC RECOMMENDS support for the Transport Security Model with TLS/DTLS. Implementations SHOULD provide the SNMPv3 security features, those claiming SNMPv3 compliance MUST support authentication and privacy through the User-based Security Model with the AES cipher, and deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED.
sections.eli5: The dials can break the whole network if the wrong person turns them, and the list of neighbors is a handy map for an attacker. So only trusted, verified people should get to read or change them.
